name: Foundation Runtime, Persistence, Migrations, Audit
not_owned_here: Local Administrator verifier/KDF and session security -> LLD-12
backup artifact envelope/format/writer/publication/recovery UX -> LLD-12; LLD-01 only provides verified consistent database snapshot/restore mechanics
domain entity schemas and business transitions -> LLD-02..LLD-09
concrete business durable-job payload/checkpoint/retry policy -> workflow-owning LLD; LLD-01 owns coordinator mechanics only
transaction_boundaries: Authoritative domain mutations enter through ExecuteAuthoritativeCommand and exactly one LLD-01 UnitOfWork; nested participant commits are forbidden.

SQLite/SQLCipher authoritative writes use short explicit transactions; operator interaction, expensive parsing, external/file work and background handler execution stay outside long-lived write transactions.

Migration application executes under exclusive canonical data-instance ownership and each accepted migration advances the migration ledger only with its schema mutation in the same governed migration transaction.

Durable-job claims, checkpoints and terminal transitions use bounded technical transactions; accepted domain mutations are delegated to owning-domain commands rather than being fabricated by job state.
failure_modes: canonical data-instance ownership cannot be proven or the instance layout is unsafe
SQLCipher/security provider cannot key and verify the authoritative connection before schema access
migration manifest/hash/ledger/schema verification detects drift, future version or integrity failure
command_id replay conflicts with command type or canonical request hash
authoritative mutation/audit/receipt work fails before commit and the UnitOfWork rolls back completely
SQLite busy/commit failure surfaces a stable foundation error without partial authoritative state
stale running durable jobs from a prior run are recovered from durable checkpoints according to their registered job contracts, never resumed from arbitrary in-memory position
shutdown/quiescence prevents new claims and leaves interrupted work recoverable
review_evidence: stable internal-to-public error mapping is explicit
authoritative command, migration and shutdown command aggregates have been split into V2-sized leaves
durable running-job claim recovery is represented explicitly
offline migration/status race-safety is represented explicitly
the packet manifest names the actual post-split algorithm and command files rather than removed aggregate filenames
LLD-12 remains the security-key and backup-artifact owner while LLD-01 remains the connection/UoW/migration/snapshot-mechanics owner
Foundation durable-job coordination has an explicit empty concrete-job registry and workflow-owning packets register their own versioned job contracts
migration sequence 1 now deterministically allocates every Foundation table/index/append-only trigger
runtime/job transitions, exact implementation destinations and forward/reverse traceability are machine-readable
design_principle: Foundation code exposes small owned interfaces; domains never import SQLite tables or web-framework internals directly. Security material is supplied through the LLD-12 provider boundary and never becomes LLD-01 domain data.
